verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. The first and third formulas are literal matches; the second needs one rewriting, for the factor ε. (a) Ψ_* = T_1 γ_d: `streamPotential` is `divideRadius (physicalCompact … (weightedSource γd))` = R⁻¹ I_c(R γ_d), which is T_1 of (8.6) with e = 1 (its docstring says so). (b) Δγ = (D_r + 1/R)Ψ_*: `streamGamma k v Ψ = graphDr k v Ψ + divideRadius Ψ` = D_rΨ + Ψ/R, term for term. The second equality Δγ = γ_d − A_1 γ_d is `streamGamma_eq_desired_sub_alias_global`, whose right-hand side is γ_d − physicalAlias(R γ_d)/R = γ_d − R⁻¹(∂_R χ_m) J(R γ_d) = γ_d − A_1 γ_d, with the paper's sign; it holds at every p including the axis p.1 = 0. (c) Δβ = −ε ∂_Z Ψ_*: `streamBeta w Ψ = -graphDz w Ψ = -fderiv Ψ p (0, w)` carries no ε, and no separate axial coordinate — the axial derivative is the derivative along a fixed direction vector w. The ε is carried in that direction vector at the use sites: `meanClass_scaledTemporalStreamBeta` forms `streamBeta (ε n • w) Ψ_*`, and `streamBeta_smul_direction` proves `streamBeta (r • w) f = r • streamBeta w f`, so `streamBeta (ε • w) Ψ_* = -ε ∂_w Ψ_*`, which is the paper's Δβ; the resulting class is α + 1, matching the paper's 'Δβ ∈ M_{α+1}'. The rewriting is one application of `streamBeta_smul_direction` (linearity of `fderiv` in the direction).
